items.authors: Ioannis Contopoulos, Spyros Rigas

items.authors: Ekaterina O. Pozdeeva, Sergey Yu. Vernov
items.abstract: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). items.authors: Rosy Caliri, Manuel Kunkel, Werner Porod
items.abstract: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. items.authors: Xuao Zhang
items.abstract: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

items.authors: Piotr Koc
items.abstract: Vacuum initial data for pure gravitational waves on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (Brill waves) have so far been obtained only numerically. items.authors: Yiling Chen, Jiayue Yang, Zhen Zhong, Robert B. Mann, Jie Jiang, Ming Zhang
items.abstract: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Ba\~nados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. items.authors: Cheng-Wei Chiang, Van Que Tran

items.abstract: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. items.abstract: Intrinsic alignments of galaxies, long regarded as a systematic in weak lensing, are now recognized as a cosmological probe complementary to galaxy clustering. items.abstract: Once the number of massless fermion flavours reaches a critical value $N_f^*$, many-flavour QCD enters the conformal window, where chiral symmetry remains unbroken in the vacuum. items.authors: Enrico Bertuzzo, Michele Frigerio, Salvador Urrea
items.abstract: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. items.authors: Jo\~ao V. Bulh\~oes, Victor P. Goncalves
items.abstract: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.

items.title: Electromagnetic Memory as a Collider Observable
items.authors: Felipe Diaz, Hern\'an A. Gonz\'alez, Oriana Labrin, Jakob Salzer
items.abstract: Electromagnetic memory and charge correlators are measured by different detectors, sensitive to soft radiation and to hard charged tracks. We show that the Ward identity of large gauge symmetry relates these quantities as inclusive observables. For lepton pairs produced by an electromagnetic current, we compute all massless multipoint memory correlators and the massive two-point function, whose coincident limit gives the soft photon number. The correlators admit a celestial free-boson representation and remain finite at first radiative order, where recoil generates back-to-back Sudakov logarithms.

items.authors: Ivan Markin, Natalie Williams, Tim Dietrich
items.abstract: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. items.title: Four consistent estimates of $H_0$ from a $\Lambda$CDM inference network given CMB data
items.authors: Gabriel P. Lynch, Lloyd Knox
items.abstract: We organize inferences from cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, of the current rate of expansion, $H_0$, into a network whose structure is informed by a scaling symmetry of the Einstein-Boltzmann evolution equations. There are four distinct routes through this network from a calibrating anchor to $H_0$. Given key assumptions of the $\Lambda$CDM model, they are mutually consistent. This consistency is a significant feature of the $\Lambda$CDM model's compatibility with CMB data. The redundancy in $H_0$ determinations illuminates a hurdle to resolving the $H_0$ tension with alternative cosmological models.

items.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. items.abstract: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. items.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
items.authors: Mathias Braun
items.abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,\alpha}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,\alpha}$ is of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$.

items.authors: Hibiki Shibuya, Yuji Terashima

Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. items.authors: Yu-Hang Jin, Xudong He, Yu Chen
items.abstract: We show that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from commutator linear responses alone. items.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
items.authors: Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric H{\'e}lein (IMJ-PRG)
items.abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.

items.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
items.authors: Tadahiro Taniguchi, Koji Hashimoto, Ryuichiro Ishikawa
items.abstract: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. items.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
items.authors: Paul Gaudin, Cl\'ement Berthi\`ere
items.abstract: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches.
